The response by type of failure: typed at the capture review on the process update and never on a person; a basic failure is met with the process's placement fixed and reaches a person only as a hypothesis at the check-in after recurrence on the same seat with the placement already fixed; a complex failure is met with the process fix only and has no person in it; an intelligent failure, a range used inside its limit and wrong, is met with the system learning and the person not corrected, and reaches the check-in only if the person brings it, because correcting it as an error is the tight edge closing. name: The slot and the gathering as communication surfaces, the Thursday hour's paragraph, and canon's lexicon against a peer's recognition
text_content:
Routed to: S11 (86ajgmj7c)

Session 10 designed the brief's team slot and the gathering's team-making half as the only two spoken surfaces the roster and the house hear beyond the operational spines, and both refuse any announcement of a structure change, because a change reaches the team by four channels and never by announcement (S8 P49). Session 11 inherits three things. The internal communication depth of both surfaces, including whether the slot's "what the system learned" item and the gathering's "what the house learned" item are governed by the transparency line (86akh5uby), and the destinations page (A9) as a page in the team's languages. The paragraph under "Thursday afternoon: one hour" (Book p.331) and the rest of Stripe's leadership cadence, which Session 10 answered only from the heading: the leads have no second weekly meeting and the partners' review has no creator hour. And finding 20.10: canon's forbidden lexicon is "in all contexts, no exceptions" (Canon 1.0, section 09) and the record's peer recognition is written by the team "in the moment" (WP p.19) and read aloud at the brief; whether a person's own words on the platform are a brand surface is unstated, and Session 10 reads the language constant as applying and the lexicon as not, marked held. This extends 86akhcz6y and 86akh67xk and does not repeat them. Filed by Session 10 of the Scaling People translation program. Session task 86ajgmj2u. Reasoning lives on the S10 page of the Sŏn Operating System doc 2ky45bmy-17253.

comment.text: Session 11 answered all three. The slot's "what the system learned" and the gathering's "what the house learned" are process and never a person or a figure, so both fall inside the part of the transparency line the team closes (shared at the moment it is versioned, to every period, in every house language) and neither is governed by the founder-gated line; the destinations page exists in every house language before the first cohort's why block because it is delivered there, and the architecture page is its parent. The Thursday hour's paragraph changes nothing: its personal round is the vulnerability prompt Session 10 refused and its topic list is the leads' review's fixed agenda derived from the closes and the lead's note; the leads have no second meeting and the partners' creator hour is the pre-opening review and the annual block; the quarterly offsite is answered by S10 P17. Finding 20.10: Session 11 holds Session 10's reading that the language constant applies to a peer's words and the lexicon does not, extends it to the check-in line, the capture's free field, and a channel item, and adds that the house-written parts of the same surfaces carry canon in full; it files a sibling finding that canon splits speech from writing once and the brief is speech reading a record, so a peer's word spoken by the room's owner is a change of speaker canon's owner must rule on. comment.text: Session 11 took all four halves. Crisis inward: a live risk reaches the house in two ways only, as a change line item with the record's three-part reason (what happened, the real impact, the fix or that there is none yet) where it changes what the roster does tonight, and as a versioned statement on the team home in every house language spoken at the next brief where it touches the house whole; otherwise it stays on the partners' page; nothing is said before it is written, and a public statement reaches the team home before or at the moment it publishes. The unblocking practice: either party's duty to write; one joint half-page (the problem as the outcome for the customer or the house, the options, the trade-offs) under the six tests; decided by the range's owner inside one domain, as a Class B hold across domains, as Class C between the leads, never up a line; on the record by the next leads' review and decided with its reason within the loop-closure window; an owner refuses a unilateral case until the absent party has been asked to write. The four-channel order in practice: the stack places the affected person's check-in before the version publishes and the entry waits for it, the person hears the reason as the evidence line's words, the sheet publishes in every house language, every open period's brief speaks one sentence under the change line, the team home shows it, and a change-reach record proves each step. Events: once the founders rule who holds one, its internal telling is the menu turn's through the three channels ahead of first service and its public telling the brand cadence's classes; until then an event is a service on the book and nothing is announced. S11 page, sections 10 and 11; P25, P26, P28, P29.

name: One account of each seat, read by three systems, and the readiness test now stands at fifty-nine rows
text_content:
Routed to: Session 17 (86ajgmk27)

Session 5's central structural claim is an assembly claim: the seat sheet that opens a seat is the same document as the seat's documented competency requirements that the invisible advocate reads, so the hiring read and the advancement read are made against one account. Three systems consume it: a candidate reads it before the first interview, the training platform's first unlock cites its version number, and the team home carries it in every language the team speaks. If the wiki lets a second account of a seat exist anywhere, skill invisibility returns in a subtler form. Session 17 assembles the seat sheet, the transparency sheet, the mutual-commitments document, the decision-rights entries, and the seat inventory into the wiki with every mark intact, keeps the cross-references between them live rather than copied, and carries the held fields as held rather than filling them by analogy. Readiness rows 36 to 59 bring the test to fifty-nine rows; five of the new rows carry a founder-gated hold inside them and two carry a partial hold, and a held row is read as failed at a gate review and never as waived. Nothing on the page is final and nothing is landed.

Provenance: Session 5, session task 86ajgmhm4, page sections 4.1, 13, and 14 (P11, P65, P66, I2, I20, I25), Operating System doc 2ky45bmy-17253.

name: The founders are the first interviewers, and their read is a scorecard rather than a review
text_content:
Routed to: Session 16 (86ajgmjz6)

Her rule is that a founder interviews every finalist and models the no on the candidate who is just fine, the hard-to-name concern. Session 5 kept the founder in the process and refused that no. Pre-opening the founder stage is the last scored stage for every seat, run in the check-in's form of length and place, reading two things only: the non-negotiables, and whether the building can supply what this person needs. Its scorecard is submitted independently and read by the domain lead who decides, like every other. A founder's no names a read or is not a no, and a founder who wants a candidate the lead declined has a structure question for the partners' review rather than a hiring one. The team recommends the stage ends for edge seats at the mechanism reset after dinner's first quarter and continues for lead seats permanently. Two things route to Session 16 specifically: what a founder's own read actually is, since the record gives the founders no training and no anchors and names the founders as the only interviewers pre-opening; and what a partner brings to a table as the customer the house is built around, since the dinner in the room reads exactly that in a candidate and the partners run it.

Provenance: Session 5, session task 86ajgmhm4, page sections 10.1 and 15 (P53, P54, I13, finding 15.13), Operating System doc 2ky45bmy-17253.

name: A departure opens a seat, and the pool is read before anyone looks outside
text_content:
Routed to: Session 15 (86ajgmjpw)

Managing out produces a departure, and a departure at Sŏn is a tension re-establishment and not a backfill: thread removal is tension loss, not slot vacancy. Session 5 fixed what happens next. The domain lead may open the seat the day the departure is known, provided the ready-now pool has been read first and the sheet records the reading, and the sheet's field 15 states what the departing node held, because the adjacent nodes are already compensating. If the pool holds someone on the track, that person's practical assessment is the next stage rather than an external search, and for a critical-path seat they take the seat's paid practical in a real service before they hold it, scored like any candidate's, because the floor will not honor a paper readiness. The succession commitment binds from the first tension loss after dinner opens, and an outside hire for any lead seat after dinner's first quarter carries a written line on the partners' page stating that no one in the pool is on the track and how far the nearest person is. Session 15's managing-out design should end where that line begins, and should not let an exit produce a seat opened externally with the pool unread.

Provenance: Session 5, session task 86ajgmhm4, page section 11.2 (P60, P61, I24), Operating System doc 2ky45bmy-17253.

name: Hiring assessments never become a person's record, and one hire arrives with a written line the check-in reads
text_content:
Routed to: Session 14 (86ajgmjk1)

Session 5 closed the packet at the hire and kept it in the applicant system: no scorecard, no assessment content, and no verdict travels to the person page, so a performance conversation months later reads what the person and their lead wrote at check-ins and never what an interviewer thought before the person started. Session 14's performance work must not reach back for the hiring record. One exception travels deliberately and is not an assessment: the candidate's own answer to the fourth read, what they said they need from the building, written on the page at the offer as the baseline the first check-in reads against. And one case arrives already flagged: where a domain lead hired against a founder's fourth-read concern, the lead writes on the packet what the building will supply that the founder said it could not, that line goes to the partners' review record, and the person's first check-in reads it. Session 14 says what happens when the building did not supply it, which is a building failure and not the person's.

Provenance: Session 5, session task 86ajgmhm4, page sections 4.5, 12.4, and 14 (P16, I14, I23), Operating System doc 2ky45bmy-17253.

name: The compensation architecture sits on the hiring timeline's critical path, and the salaried line decides who gets a last round
text_content:
Routed to: Session 13 (86ajgmjey)

The record's transparency sheet is handed at the first interview with everything needed to decide, including the compensation mechanics, and the record elsewhere says the mechanics are still being finalized. The leads are in the building at least six weeks before dinner's gate, so their first interviews fall months before Session 13 can ratify the architecture: the record's own sheet cannot be handed as specified until it lands. That makes the architecture a hiring gate and not a parallel track, and the record does not say so. Session 5 states the record's compensation commitments on the sheet and no architecture, carries no figure and no percentage anywhere, and recommends that the mechanics field may read "being finalized" for the pre-opening leads' first interviews and never for an offer; the founders rule on that interim. Session 13 also decides which seats are salaried, because the record's last round, the dinner in the room, applies to leadership and salaried seats, so the salaried line decides who gets one. And cross-strand fluency's recognition is already an open item in the record; Session 5 adds cross-period fluency beside it (see the Session 8 and Session 13 carryover on that marker).

Provenance: Session 5, session task 86ajgmhm4, page sections 7.4, 7.5, and 15 (P34, P35, finding 15.3, readiness rows 46 and 47), Operating System doc 2ky45bmy-17253.

name: Recruiting hands Session 12 two feedback events it does not yet know how to deliver
text_content:
Routed to: Session 12 (86ajgmjba)

Two of recruiting's triggers are performance feedback to a person in the house, and Session 5 fixed where they go and not how they are given. First, a scorecard returned without a named read goes to the Maitre d as a re-training trigger, and the interviewer does not run another stage until the re-training is done; that is the tell of an untrained interviewer, and it is also a lead or a team member being told their work was not good enough. Second, a decline at the packet that contradicts every stage's scorecard goes to the leads' review as a calibration read, which puts one person's judgment in front of the other lead. Session 12 designs how both are delivered inside the check-in's form and the leads' review's, without turning either into a verdict, and says what the lead does when the pattern repeats. The constraint from Session 4 holds: the lead may not write on the person page outside a check-in, and neither of these events is a check-in.

Provenance: Session 5, session task 86ajgmhm4, page sections 9.3 and 12.2 to 12.3 (P52, I21), Operating System doc 2ky45bmy-17253.

name: Every recruiting surface is bound by canon rules whose register canon does not name, and by the languages the house speaks
text_content:
Routed to: Session 11 (86ajgmj7c)

Canon is the source of truth for every word, its language constant applies in any internal communication, and its forbidden lexicon applies in all contexts with no exceptions, yet its register matrix names six surfaces and none of them is a recruiting or employee-facing surface; "you" is specified for customer-facing contexts, and a candidate reading a posting is not a customer in that moment; and canon does not say whether a document handed to a candidate is a brand context, which decides whether the Korean terms stand unglossed in front of a stranger. The team read one register and could only mark it held for canon's owner. Alongside it sits a set of language obligations Session 11 owns: the seat sheet lives on the team home in every language the team speaks, the transparency sheet is handed in the candidate's interview language, every stage is run by someone who speaks the language the candidate chose, the answer set exists in every language the process runs in, and every posting states which languages the process itself is available in. Session 11 designs the communication system those obligations run on and closes what it can of the register question with canon's owner.

Provenance: Session 5, session task 86ajgmhm4, page sections 5.4, 14, and 15 (P22, I3, I5, I15, finding 15.5), Operating System doc 2ky45bmy-17253.

name: The record holds inclusion mechanics and no position on who the team is
text_content:
Routed to: Session 11 (86ajgmj7c)

The record protects dignity through interview language choice, asks in every interview whether the building is equipped to create the environment this person needs to succeed, and measures engagement across psychological safety and values alignment. It states no goal, no read, and no position on the composition of the team, and canon's non-negotiables are conduct constraints rather than composition ones. Her chapter treats referral-driven homogeneity as first-order and her workbook scores a recruiter on it, and each of the record's own four sources narrows: the founders' reach, the referral, and a build audience that self-selects. Session 5 did not assert a position for the house. It recommended the read any position would need, running regardless: source-dominance and stage-rate data read at the leads' review, with no target and no figure, checked at readiness row 58. name: An open seat is a load reading on a domain, and a departure is a tension re-establishment
text_content:
Routed to: Session 9 (86ajgmj07)

Session 5 routed recruiting's failures into the diagnostic cadence rather than into a recruiting scoreboard. A seat open past its response window with no candidate advanced goes to the leads' review as a load reading on the domain, not as a recruiting failure. A seat open past three consecutive leads' reviews goes to the partners' review as a possible node-overload entry, because the adjacent nodes have been compensating for three weeks. A seat the lead wants to hold open rather than fill below the bar goes to the leads' review as a slack reading, since the bar holds only if the house can absorb the hole at tempo. A seat opened by tension loss goes to that week's leads' review as one line: what the node held and what the adjacent nodes are carrying, because a departure is a tension re-establishment problem and not a backfill problem. And a decline at the packet that contradicts every stage's scorecard goes to the leads' review as a calibration read, not as an appeal. Session 9's diagnostic method should read these as signals of the same kind as the five failure modes scorecard, and should say what a diagnosis does with a domain that produces them repeatedly.

Provenance: Session 5, session task 86ajgmhm4, page sections 4.4, 6.3, 8.6, and 12.3 (P14, P28, P46, I22), Operating System doc 2ky45bmy-17253.

name: Cross-period fluency is the second development marker the record needs and does not name
text_content:
Routed to: Session 8 (86ajgmhxx), Session 13 (86ajgmjey)

The record names cross-strand fluency as the real development marker, makes it visible in the web as more connections, and recognizes it in compensation as meaningful, with its recognition a named open item. Everything else in the record requires a second marker: one restaurant and one brand met at different times of day, late night as dinner's own later register, one system and four moods, same foundation and four registers, each period continuing the one before it. All of it asks the same person to hold a different register at a different hour. Recruiting hit this because one labor pool staffs the service periods, the seat sheet's service-period field is where a person's second period is recorded, and the first period expansion is the first succession event, so the dinner cohort is being hired into a fluency the record has not named. Session 5 recommends naming cross-period fluency as a development marker parallel to cross-strand fluency, recorded on the person page as connections. Session 8 places it structurally; Session 13 decides whether it is recognized in compensation, alongside cross-strand fluency's own open recognition.

Provenance: Session 5, session task 86ajgmhm4, page sections 11.3 and 15 (P62, finding 15.1), Operating System doc 2ky45bmy-17253.

name: No runner or host seat can be opened until the inward-facing floor strand has a lead
text_content:
Routed to: Session 8 (86ajgmhxx)

The record names the inward-facing floor strand and names no domain owner for it, while naming Station Leads in the kitchen and the Head of Beverage in beverage. A runner's seat sits between the Maitre d's team development and the Operations Lead's operational outcomes, and the Lead Host is a functional designation and not a permanent elevation, so it is not a domain lead in the hiring sense; the team reads hosts as the Maitre d's domain and marks it held against the open question of whether the floor manager and the Maitre d are one role or two. Session 8's team-structures work closes the structural half; the founders close the naming (filed as a work item). name: There is no seat inventory, and three artifacts hold three different lists of what seats exist
text_content:
Routed to: Session 8 (86ajgmhxx)

Recruiting cannot open a seat that is not on an inventory, every inventory seat's competency requirements must exist before the cohort arrives so a person on the first day can see the seat after theirs, and readiness row 36 walks a training service's schedule against the inventory name by name. The white paper names seats in prose and calls role naming an open item, canon's uniform system names five roles, and the deck names five different ones, dropping hosts and the daytime role and adding the runner; "daytime" is a seat for a period without a ratified charter. Session 8 holds the inventory's structure and reconciles the three lists.

name: The work style grid is out of recruiting and may return only as a self-awareness tool
text_content:
Routed to: Session 7 (86ajgmhrz), Session 10 (86ajgmj2u)

Her grid crosses introvert and extrovert with task and people orientation to produce Analyzer, Director, Collaborator, and Promoter. Session 5 kept it out of recruiting entirely: not as a scorecard attribute, not as an interview question, not as a team-composition target. The reasoning was structural rather than cultural. Service pressure selects hard for assertion and expression, the people interviewing are the people the room rewarded, and a hiring system that lets the room's read stand as the hiring read reproduces the room; the answer is inward-facing seats opened and filled on their own competency requirements with equal rigor and never as a step toward outward-facing seats, measurement held by the stack and accounted for by the Operations Lead, and the paid practical scored by rubric by an assessor who does not decide. The grid may return inside the house as a self-awareness tool, and where it returns is Session 7's and Session 10's to place. If either session brings it back, it comes back as language people use about themselves and never as an instrument that reads a person for a seat.

Provenance: Session 5, session task 86ajgmhm4, page sections 3.4 and 14 (P8, P9, I26), Operating System doc 2ky45bmy-17253.

name: The person page exists before the first shift, and the start date has conditions
text_content:
Routed to: Session 7 (86ajgmhrz)

Recruiting creates the person page at the offer accepted, not at the first shift, and writes ten entries to it and nothing else: the seat and its sheet version, the strand, the domain lead by seat, the decision-rights range as accepted, the service periods, the start date, the mentor connected before arrival, the ninety-day plan's start, the first unlock the sheet names, and what the candidate said they need from the building, in their own words, captured at the first interview as the fourth read. That last entry is the baseline the first check-in's "what is in the way" question reads against, and Session 7 designs the ninety-day plan so its six check-ins carry it. No assessment scorecard ever travels to the page; the packet closes at the hire and its record stays in the applicant system. The start date carries conditions a lead may not commit against: the mentor is connected, the uniform and locker are ready, the training platform carries the seat's first modules, the ninety-day plan's first check-in falls on a pre-service window the lead works, the mechanics field is filled, and the person's first shift is not a new period's first service and is not coverage before the record's own bar that no one touches a table until they are ready. A start date that cannot be set inside a month of acceptance because the mentor or the modules are not ready is a training-infrastructure load, not a recruiting one.

Provenance: Session 5, session task 86ajgmhm4, page sections 4.5 and 12.6 (P16, I23), Operating System doc 2ky45bmy-17253.

name: What Session 6 inherits as settled, and the five instruments it must not build
text_content:
Routed to: Session 6 (86ajgmhnt)

Session 5 closed the decision structure that Session 6's hiring loop runs inside, and Session 6 should extend it rather than reopen it. There is no hiring committee and no hiring meeting: the decision is the domain lead's, on a complete packet of independently submitted scorecards, made the day the packet completes, with the answer sent the same day, and Greenhouse refuses a decision on an incomplete packet. There is no recruiting seat: the coordination is the stack's, the candidate-experience standard is the Maitre d's, the record is the Operations Lead's. No assessor decides and no decider assesses alone; a decline names a read or a must-have from the sheet and nothing else; a lead who is one of two first-interview interviewers requires the second. A hole is held rather than filled below the bar, and the leads' review carries it as a slack question. Five instruments are refused with the mechanism that does their work named in each case: her work style grid (which may return only as a self-awareness tool in onboarding or team development, never in the interview), the résumé review and the take-home, the hiring committee and the hiring meeting, her recruiter's interview loop and scorecard, and the bias-neutralizing copy tool.

Provenance: Session 5, session task 86ajgmhm4, page sections 8.6, 9.1, and 14 (P8, P40, P46, P48, P68, I26 to I30), Operating System doc 2ky45bmy-17253.

name: The hiring timeline runs against gates, not dates, and three of them are upstream of any hire
text_content:
Routed to: Session 6 (86ajgmhnt)

Session 6 places the hiring calendar, and three sequences bind it. The chef is first: under either branch of the chef ruling the kitchen pipeline runs as a chain with no link skippable, ruling, chef in the seat, canon's Session 1B, menu, kitchen seat sheets, kitchen practicals, kitchen hires, their training, dinner's gate, and until the chef is seated and the menu exists there is nothing for a kitchen practical to reproduce. The two leads are in the building at least six weeks before dinner's gate, because the leads' review must have run six consecutive weeks with records, and the pipeline read must have run as a standing line at six consecutive leads' reviews. And the compensation architecture sits on the critical path: the transparency sheet is handed at the first interview with the mechanics on it, the leads' first interviews fall months before Session 13 can ratify the architecture, and no offer is made and no start date committed on a sheet whose mechanics field is unfilled. Session 6 places the architecture's ratification on the hiring calendar rather than treating it as a parallel track. A practical is never scheduled to make a start date; that rule is the seam protection, and a date-driven practical puts build tempo into the room.

Provenance: Session 5, session task 86ajgmhm4, page sections 8.4, 10.3, and 15 (P42, P58, findings 15.3 and 15.9, readiness rows 42, 56, 59), Operating System doc 2ky45bmy-17253.

name: The first interviewers are untrained by the record's own definition
text_content:
Routed to: Session 6 (86ajgmhnt)

The record requires trained interviewers, because asking a good question and reading the answer is a learned skill and not an instinct that arrives with a title. The training infrastructure is the learning platform on which any qualified team member creates modules, and the platform does not exist before the team does. Pre-opening the founders are the only interviewers, then the two leads, and nothing in the record trains any of them, so the first hires of the house are made by untrained interviewers under the record's own definition. This is not a detail: readiness row 44 requires a training record on a person page before any stage runs, and the training record instrument requires one for every partner before the first stage. Session 6 writes the training's content and, with the founders, writes how the first interviewers are trained before the platform exists. The re-training trigger is already fixed: a scorecard returned without a named read sends the interviewer back before their next stage.

Provenance: Session 5, session task 86ajgmhm4, page section 15, finding 15.13 (with P52 and I21), Operating System doc 2ky45bmy-17253.

name: The assessment rubric's structure is fixed; Session 6 fills it and adds nothing to it
text_content:
Routed to: Session 6 (86ajgmhnt)

Role definition sits in recruiting, upstream of sourcing and upstream of Session 6's interview loop, and the seat sheet that opens a seat is the same document as the seat's documented competency requirements that the invisible advocate reads. Session 5 specified the rubric as field 8 of that sheet: the stages by class (every seat takes application, first interview, decision, answer; high-volume seats add the phone screen, physical-skill seats the paid practical, leadership and salaried seats the dinner in the room, domain-owner seats an adjacent-domain second interviewer, and pre-opening every seat adds the founder stage), the four reads assigned per stage and no other, the must-haves and disqualifiers from the sheet's fields 6 and 9, who may run each stage and who may not, the scorecard's shape, and the rule that a scorecard carries no free-text verdict. Session 6 writes what goes inside that structure: the documented questions per stage, the answer anchors that say what evidence for each read looks like at entry level, the interviewer training that teaches the questions and the anchors, and the calibration that keeps the read consistent across interviewers. Session 6 does not add a read, a stage, a runner, or a verdict column, does not rebuild the structure, and does not open a rubric for a seat that has no sheet.

Provenance: Session 5, session task 86ajgmhm4, page sections 4.1 and 14 (P11, P67, I7), Operating System doc 2ky45bmy-17253.

comment.text: Session 12 designed the three things this item asked for. How the lead coaches: by hypothesis, from records the person can read, with the hypothesis having no page, said once at the check-in after the person's own account, as an open-ended question about a specific service and then an observation of behavior and impact owned as the lead's perception, with the person's line as the only residue. The conflict between S4 P18's "said in person between check-ins" and S10 P15's "the check-in's" is surfaced for the founders with the narrowing recommended. S12 page, sections 3 to 6; P4 to P10, P12 to P19.

name: The principles are what feedback and review reference
text_content:
Routed to: S12 (86ajgmjba), S13 (86ajgmjey)

Why S12 and S13 need it. Her test for principles is that they are "truly expressed in how we hire, reward, lead, and conduct ourselves across the company." A principle that nothing references is decoration.

The charter's principles are the standard Session 12's feedback and coaching system references and Session 13's formal review measures. Both sessions design against the principles as ratified rather than inventing a separate behavioral standard, and both should flag any principle that cannot be observed in behavior, because such a principle fails her deliverability test and should go back to the charter rather than be worked around.

This is also the check on Session 2's own recommendation that principles be drawn from decisions rather than moments. If a decision-derived principle turns out to be unobservable on the floor, the revision cadence (86akh3unw) is where it gets fixed.

name: Cross-strand fluency: S8 defines it, S13 prices it
text_content:
Routed to: S8 (86ajgmhxx), S13 (86ajgmjey)

Why S8 and S13 need it. The record makes a compensation commitment it has not defined well enough to pay against. Cross-strand fluency, the ability to hold the outward-facing and inward-facing work at once, "has genuine additional value, visible in the web as more connections and recognized in compensation as meaningful" (WP p. 11). The white paper's own open items list "Compensation architecture, how cross-strand fluency is recognized and paid" as a separate deliverable (WP p. 15).

The commitment is in the charter. The definition and the price are not, and they belong to different sessions.

Session 8 owns the definition: what a strand is, what fluency across strands means in observable terms, and how it is demonstrated rather than asserted. Without that, Session 13 is pricing a quality nobody can assess.

Session 13 owns the premium: how the point system recognizes it, against the commitments confirmed in the charter.

name: Onboarding delivers the charter's mission, principles, and behavioral standard before operational training
text_content:
Routed to: S7 (86ajgmhrz)

Why S7 needs it. The record already commits to this sequence: "Why comes before how. Orientation to the mission, the values, and the behavioral standard happens before operational training, because a person needs the reason before the mechanics" (WP p. 20).

Those three things are the operating charter's mission, principles, and non-negotiables. Session 7 designs onboarding to deliver them in that order, drawing the content from the charter rather than writing its own version.

And the flag Session 7 must raise if it still applies. Onboarding cannot orient a new employee to a mission that does not exist. If the charter is unratified when Session 7 runs, Session 7 records that the record's own onboarding commitment is unmet and names the charter as its blocking dependency rather than filling the gap with brand language. This is the same debt Session 2 identified: the record committed to delivering founding documents to every new hire before those documents were written.

name: Compensation commitments are what recruiting states; the architecture waits for S13
text_content:
Routed to: S5 (86ajgmhm4), S6 (86ajgmhnt), S13 (86ajgmjey)

Why these sessions need it. Session 2 was asked whether the compensation philosophy belongs in the charter or waits for S13, and recommends splitting it. The commitments go in the charter, because they are founding commitments and because every hiring session needs them to score against. The architecture goes to S13.

The commitments the record already holds, stated case by case and never as a philosophy: labor as an asset rather than a cost to minimize; the company pays for what matters and does not shift costs to employees; dignity as a precondition for presence; compensation built into price, never a tip, never a service charge, and never presented as one; distributed to the whole team including the kitchen; no hierarchy of importance; cross-strand fluency recognized in pay; benefits planned from the start.

Sessions 5 and 6 state those commitments in recruiting and hiring material. The record's own hiring design already requires it: the candidate receives a single sheet carrying compensation, benefits, and the compensation mechanics. Sessions 5 and 6 do not state or imply a percentage.

Session 13 builds the architecture against the same commitments once Dominic has reviewed the list: percentage, point weights, daily calculation, payment rhythm, and the cross-strand premium.

No figure is carried anywhere in this chain. The record states the embedded percentage is still being finalized, and financials are not a context source for this program. A figure-dependent read is a stated gap.

name: The daypart charter is the phased-opening gate and the form the lunch decision takes
text_content:
Routed to: S4 (86ajgmhjr), S8 (86ajgmhxx)

Why S4 and S8 need it. Session 2 found that her team charter does not map to Sŏn. Her unit is a team inside a division inside a company; Sŏn has strands, domains, two parallel leads, and four service periods. Session 2 recommends Sŏn deliberately does not use team charters, and uses a daypart charter instead: one page per service period, covering its reason to exist, first customer, leading-indicator measures, what it gives the connective layer, what would make it a worse version of dinner, what it hands on, and its operating logic.

Session 4 places the drafting and ruling of a daypart charter on the cadence ahead of each opening, so that no service period opens without one. This gives the record's phased opening (dinner alone for at least a quarter, then early morning, then late night) a written gate rather than a schedule.

Session 8 uses the charter's operating-logic section to design how authority and pace differ by period without adding leadership lines, which is the constraint the record's eight-line leadership structure sits under.

It is also the form the lunch decision takes. The record holds that whether lunch is built at all is an equal three-partner decision and a real option to remove. A lunch charter that cannot be written without describing a worse version of dinner is the record's "no good answer for lunch," reached structurally.

name: Principles version one is pre-opening and carries a mandatory revision cadence
text_content:
Routed to: S4 (86ajgmhjr)

Why S4 needs it. Her method for drafting principles is to write down notable moments in the company's history and ask what belief prevailed in them. Sŏn has no operating history, so version one of the principles is drawn from decisions already in the record rather than from moments.

That is a sound way to start and an unsound way to finish. Her own warning is that principles disconnected from how the company actually operates do not resonate, and a pre-opening company cannot yet test the connection.

Session 4 places a mandatory principles revision on the operating cadence at two points: after dinner has run alone for its first quarter, which the record sets as the phased opening's first gate, and after the first full year. At each, the principles are tested against moments the company has actually had.

name: Long-term commitments parent every metric, and the metric layer is leading indicators
text_content:
Routed to: S3 (86ajgmhgx), S4 (86ajgmhjr)

Why S3 and S4 need it. The charter carries long-term commitments without figures, and every metric and goal Sessions 3 and 4 set must ladder up to one of them. That is her structure and Session 2 recommends keeping it.

The constraint Sŏn adds: the record rejects the conventional measures as the primary read. "Revenue, labor percentage, food cost: these exist because they have always existed. All lagging indicators. By the time they signal a problem, the damage is done" (WP p. 22). It names three leading indicators instead: employee NPS, cultural labor score, and customer recognition rate, plus the cultural measures at WP p. 23 (retention rate, internal promotion rate, engagement across psychological safety and values alignment, participation in development).

Sessions 3 and 4 build the metric layer from those, and a proposed metric that is a lagging indicator has to argue for itself against the record.

No figure or target value is carried. Financials are not a context source for this program.

name: Decision-rights entries take owner, range, triggers form
text_content:
Routed to: S3 (86ajgmhgx)

Why S3 needs it. Session 3's accountability material assumes a decision-rights structure and will otherwise import one from the standard management apparatus.

It does not need to. Session 2 found that Sŏn's record already assigns decision rights at least eight times without ever stating the rule: lunch as an equal three-partner decision; sonic governance in three tiers; floor authority split between server and floor manager; the David protocol as a system decision never a floor call; the design system governed by one owner with an RFC path; naming at three-party sign-off; content at green-light, strategic review, and leadership review; and the server's authorized generosity range.

They share one shape: authority sits with the closest competent owner; the range within which that owner acts without asking is stated in advance; the triggers that escalate are named before the event rather than judged during it.

Session 3 adopts that three-part form for every decision-rights entry in the operating system, rewrites the eight existing instances into it, and treats an entry missing any part as incomplete. The rule itself is recommended by Session 2 and awaits ratification; the deadlock case remains founder-gated (86akh3ty7).

text_content:
Routed to: S8 (86ajgmhxx)

Why S8 needs it. The white paper's management layer names the co-lead who owns the how of the experience, the team, and the floor as the Maitre d, "the Hospitality Manager in full deployment," freed from the host stand (WP p.10). The canon's service model assigns floor authority to a "floor manager" who owns the room, and its uniform system lists "floor manager" as a role and "hosts" as another (canon 08). The canon's arrival choreography also places a Maître d' at the top of the porch steps. It is not clear from the record whether "floor manager" and "Maitre d" are one role under two names, or whether the canon's floor manager is a shift-level designation below the co-lead. The white paper lists role naming as an open item (WP p.15). S8, which owns team structures and already carries the chef-gated back-of-house question (86ajgmmc3), should resolve the naming before it draws the structure, so it does not draw two roles where the record holds one.

name: The nervous system does not read the center
text_content:
Routed to: S16 (86ajgmjz6)

Why S16 needs it. The record's metabolic sequence, bandwidth then joy then retention then results, is stated as mechanical and applied to the whole team, with leading indicators (employee NPS, cultural labor score) as the nervous system's read on team bandwidth (WP p.12, p.17, p.22). The cooling failure mode is named as running people at capacity and calling it dedication (WP p.13). The content engine is sized to avoid burning the founders out (WP p.30). But there is no instrument that reads the founders' own bandwidth, and the record's claim that founders are not exempt is implicit. Session 16 owns the founder's time, energy, and self-management. It designs the founder-level read, and decides who sets a founder's own learning tempo, which Session 1 could not resolve. The founders' hand-written version of this read is prompt H of their working-with-me documents.

name: The founder decision-rights rule does not exist
text_content:
Routed to: S2 (86ajgmhfd), S3 (86ajgmhgx)

Why S2 and S3 need it. The record holds that authority lives in the domain and that the founders own their domains outright. It holds one rule for a decision that crosses domains: lunch is an equal three-partner decision (WP p.36). It holds no general rule for which decisions are domain-owned, which are joint, what happens when a domain decision has consequences in another domain, or how three equal partners break a deadlock. This is distinct from the founder job descriptions (86ajgnhp7), which describe what each founder owns; this is the rule for the seams between what they own. S2's founding documents need to state it or state that it is open. S3's accountability material assumes a decision-rights structure and will otherwise import one from the standard apparatus. Each founder's draft of the rule from inside their domain is collected in prompt D of their working-with-me document; the rule itself is a founder decision filed in the post-extraction work.

name: The record holds two accounts of the chef seat
text_content:
Routed to: S2 (86ajgmhfd)

Why S2 needs it. Session 2 writes the founding documents, and the existing carryover on founder job descriptions (86ajgnhp7) will describe the chef partner's seat. The record currently describes it two ways. The white paper: the chef partner "owns the culinary vision as an equal founding partner" (WP p.03), freed from carrying the rest of the business (WP p.05), with the business explicitly not resting on any one person (WP p.37). The canon's held items, written under a heading that anticipates an executive chef hire: "The brand owns the culinary identity. The chef executes within it" (canon, what remains). These are not the same statement, and S2 cannot write the chef's founding document without knowing which governs. A founder decision to reconcile them has been filed in the post-extraction work; S2 reads the outcome if it exists, and surfaces the conflict rather than picking a side if it does not. The chef partner's own reading is invited in their working-with-me document (Session 1 page, section 7.4) and is chef-gated.

name: Who supplies what: Claude never generates Brandon's interiority or Sŏn's intent
text_content:
Status: routed, standing, governs every session including this one.

This program is an assistant, not an automation. The distinction is not a courtesy. It is a rule about what may be written down.

Claude never generates

Facts about Brandon, Dominic, or the chef partner. Values, work style, strengths, motivations, failure modes.

Facts about what Sŏn intends. Mission, vision, operating principles, what good looks like on the floor, what will and will not be tolerated.

Any decision.

Claude has memory and context sufficient to produce very plausible versions of all of the above. Plausible and unendorsed is the worst available outcome, because it reads as true, is assembled from true fragments, and gets acted on. A document about how Brandon appears is not a document about Brandon.

Claude generates

Analysis. Structure. Translation. Argument. Record.

The three-way sort: what transfers, what adapts, what does not apply, and why. Rebuilding her instruments for a different substrate: hourly, shift-based, four dayparts, embedded compensation, no headcount growth. Holding the standard when a definition goes soft. Writing it up and filing it correctly.

The rule that carries this

Claude may propose. Claude may not record a proposal as a decision.

A proposal goes in the Open section, named as awaiting Brandon. It does not go in the body as settled. S1 did this correctly with the founder 1:1 cadence: proposed weekly and quarterly, marked open, awaiting confirmation. That is the pattern.

When a session needs a decision Brandon has not made, it stops and asks. It does not propose and proceed.

The gradient

Ownership is not constant across the program.

Heavily Brandon. S1 (done). S2, founding documents. S16, founder time and energy. These are interiority and intent. Claude structures the question and refuses to answer it.

Heavily structural. S13, rebuilding compensation architecture around a 21.5% embedded share. S6, interview loop mechanics. Claude does most of the building, against decisions Brandon makes.

Joint, and this is where the value is. Brandon proposes, Claude pushes, Brandon decides. It does not work if either side is asleep.

The specific S2 trap

Brand canon is an input to the founding documents. It is not a substitute for the decision.

Sŏn's mission is a choice. It is not a synthesis of existing brand language, however elegant that synthesis would be. A Claude in S2 that assembles a mission statement out of "life share not market share," "the building is not the asset, the customer is," and the playground philosophy has committed exactly the failure this item exists to prevent.

Note on the session briefs

Several session tasks say "Sŏn output (draft): [artifact]." That phrasing hands the pen to Claude by default and it is a drafting error in the build-out, not an instruction. This item governs where it conflicts with a brief. S1 already resolved one such conflict correctly by weighting the carryover over the task. That was right.

name: Working-with-me is pre-signature diligence, not onboarding
text_content:
Routed to: S7, Ch3 Onboarding (86ajgmhrz)

She files the "Working with Me" document and the "Working with Claire" worked example in the Chapter 3 workbook, under onboarding. Her New Leader Experience schedule hands it to a leader around week nine.

S1 already decided this and S7 must not re-file it.

At Sŏn the working-with-me exchange is a founding-partner diligence artifact, exchanged before the chef signs, not an onboarding step after. A founding partner conducts more diligence than an investor. The chef is being asked to bind a career to two people they have not worked a service with.

When S7 reaches this material, it inherits the S1 decision. What S7 legitimately owns is the separate question of whether a version of this exists for salaried managers hired later, and it does not own the founder or partner case.

Also inherited from S1: the instrument must never be required of hourly floor staff. Coerced self-disclosure from someone with less power is not self-awareness. Founders and managers write these. The floor reads them.

See Sŏn Operating System, page S1, section 5.

name: Levels and ladders: does a single house need them at all
text_content:
Routed to: S8 Team structures (86ajgmhxx), S13 Formal review + compensation (86ajgmjey)

Her checklist assumes job ladders and levels, clearly communicated. Her whole review and compensation apparatus hangs off them.

Sŏn has none, and the open question is not when to build them. It is whether a single 120-seat house should have them at all.

The case against: levels in a company that does not grow are a promise the company cannot keep. They manufacture the expectation of a ladder and then supply four rungs.

The case for: without levels there is no legible answer to "what is my path," and a strong candidate will ask on day one.

Downstream of 86ajgnh8n (Sŏn does not scale to 7,000). If lateral daypart movement is the real structure, then levels may be the wrong shape entirely and something else has to carry what a ladder carries elsewhere.

Do not default to building them because the book assumes them.

Surfaced S1.

name: The 1:1 has no shift-native form: her cadence assumes desks
text_content:
Routed to: S4, Ch2 Operating cadence (86ajgmhjr). Secondary: S12 (86ajgmjba)

Her entire cadence rests on the 1:1: weekly or biweekly, rarely rescheduled, shared agenda, notes, actions, quarterly goals tracked inside it. It is the load-bearing member of her operating system.

It is written for salaried knowledge workers with desks, calendars, and control over their own hours. It does not survive contact with shift-based hourly staff who are on the clock only when the room is open and who are paid for the shift, not the meeting.

The function is not optional. The form is. S4 has to produce a shift-native equivalent or Sŏn will simply not do 1:1s, which is what almost every restaurant does.

Open questions S4 must answer:

When does it happen and is the person paid for it
What replaces the shared 1:1 document for someone who does not open documents
Is quarterly even the right unit, or are daypart and season the native cycles
Does the pre-shift lineup, which already exists daily, absorb part of this function

Note the inversion: Sŏn's problem is not too few team meetings. Lineup and family meal already happen daily. The problem is that the daily meeting carries no structure.

Surfaced S1.

name: Work style demand differs by daypart: one labor pool, four profiles
text_content:
Routed to: S5 Recruiting (86ajgmhm4), S6 Hiring (86ajgmhnt), S8 Team structures (86ajgmhxx)

Her work style grid (introvert/extrovert against task/people oriented, producing Analyzer, Director, Collaborator, Promoter) is a self-awareness tool. Used as a team-composition tool in a restaurant it produces a specific, predictable distortion: service pressure selects hard for Director and Promoter. A floor staffed by pattern-matching to the room ends up with almost no Analyzers, at which point nothing gets measured and no one notices.

The four dayparts make this sharper. They do not demand the same profile.

Good Energy, morning. Repetition, precision, prep, low interaction density, high consequence for small errors. Analyzer and Collaborator work.
Dosi, lunch. Throughput under a clock. Director work.
Dinner. The full range. The only daypart that genuinely wants all four.
Luxx, late night. Energy, presence, the room. Promoter work.

A single house running four dayparts is not staffing one work-style profile. It is staffing four, from one labor pool, with substantial overlap between them.

Interacts with 86ajgmmc3 (four dayparts is not four teams).

Surfaced S1.

name: Compensation philosophy does not exist: the structure does
text_content:
Routed to: S13, Ch5 Formal review + compensation (86ajgmjey)

Her Management Prerequisites Checklist asks whether you have a compensation philosophy and a clear framework that employees understand.

Sŏn has a structure: compensation embedded in menu pricing at a 21.5% revenue share, never surfaced as a service charge line. It has no philosophy.

A tipless house survives or fails on whether its staff can explain, in their own words, why they are paid this way and why it is better for them. Nobody has written that. Until it is written, the strongest operational commitment Sŏn has made is one its own team cannot articulate.

This is the largest live gap on the prerequisites checklist. It is also a recruiting instrument, because it is the first question any strong candidate will ask, and a wrong answer at that moment costs the hire.

Interacts with carryover 86ajgmmkd (scorecard and review rubric are one instrument, plus embedded comp) and with 86ajgnh8n (no promotion ladder to attach compensation growth to).

Surfaced S1.

name: Sŏn does not scale to 7,000: her headcount premise does not apply
text_content:
Routed to: all sessions. Read before every sort.

She wrote for a company going from 200 people to 7,000. "Scaling to the call," her frame for evaluating whether a person can grow into a larger role, only means something in a company that inflates around them.

Sŏn opens at roughly full size and stays there. A line cook in year three is a line cook in a 120-seat house. There is no org chart bloating underneath anyone. The role does not grow because the company does not.

This is not a limitation. It is a different compounding mechanism and it is Sŏn's actual thesis. Sŏn compounds in customer relationships and system knowledge, not headcount.

Consequences that must be tested in every remaining session:

Career development cannot be sold as promotion. There is no ladder above a station in a single house.
Retention is the whole game. A departure removes accumulated customer knowledge that took years to build and cannot be rehired. Her hiring chapter is calibrated for volume. Sŏn's must be calibrated for permanence.
Her review machinery sorts people for advancement. Sŏn's must deepen people in place. Different instruments wearing the same name.
The four dayparts are the only real lateral surface. Movement at Sŏn is across dayparts, not up levels.

Anything in the book that presupposes headcount growth is suspect by default.

Logged as decision D1.8, S1.

name: Specifications, not instruments: no SOPs until the document methodology exists
text_content:
Status: routed, applies to every session.

Sessions produce decisions and specifications. Sessions do not produce instruments.

Build: what Sŏn's operating system is. Binding decisions. Specifications stating what an eventual instrument must contain, do, and refuse to do.

Do not build: SOPs, worksheets, fillable templates, training modules, finished rubrics, house-format internal documents.

Why: Sŏn has no document methodology yet. Task 86ajgn2z5 establishes one, adapting Brandon's instructional design profiles to the business context. Producing instruments before that exists means seventeen sessions of good thinking rendered into seventeen inconsistent formats.

Capture is the opposite of restricted. Everything pertaining to the instruments goes into the specification, exhaustively. Her rubric structures, scoring bands, question banks, checklist logic, interview loop mechanics. What transfers clean. What breaks against embedded compensation or a four-daypart floor. What a Sŏn version would have to carry that hers does not.

Capture all of it. Build none of it.

S17, the company wiki, is a produced document and is gated on 86ajgn2z5. Sessions 1 through 16 are not.

name: The workbook is free and official: both PDFs load every session
text_content:
Status: routed, applies to every session.

Stripe Press publishes the full 100+ page workbook free: https://press.stripe.com/scaling-people/workbooks

It is the officially distributed artifact, designed to be downloaded, filled in, and adapted. It is not redundant with the book. The book carries the reasoning. The workbook carries the instruments.

Both PDFs get uploaded at the start of every session. Neither enters the context window. Both land on disk and are read by page range. Uploading a 531-page book and a 100-page workbook costs the same context as uploading nothing: zero.

Workbook structure:

Section Workbook pages
Chapter 1 3 to 10
Chapter 2 11 to 41
Chapter 3 42 to 88
Chapter 4 89 to 102
Chapter 5 103 onward
Known filing quirk: the "Working with Me" template and "Working with Claire" example sit in the Chapter 3 workbook, around pp. 80 to 85, not in Chapter 1. She files them as onboarding artifacts. Session 1 pulls them forward.

Page numbers above are her printed section markers. Verify against actual PDF pages on first upload.

name: Chef-gated BOH structure + four dayparts is not four teams
text_content:
Routed to: S8, Ch4 Team structures (86ajgmhxx)

Two things collide in S8.

Chef partner seat is open. BOH structure is that person's to shape from the beginning. Stated structural position, not a gap. Build the FOH org and the shared spine. Mark BOH chef-gated. Do not stall the session.

Four dayparts, one roof. Good Energy, Dosi, dinner, Luxx. Her team structures assume one org with one operating register. The stated thesis is that dayparts compound rather than reset, which means this is closer to four shifts of one team than four teams. That distinction has to be settled in S8, because everything about scheduling, cross-training, and identity follows from it.

Collect for the chef onboarding packet. Whatever S8 leaves open goes into the packet assembled in S17.

name: Code-bearing vs her hierarchy: reconcile or depart
text_content:
Routed to: S3, Ch2 The operating system (86ajgmhgx)

Her operating system is written for a hierarchical knowledge-work org. Brandon's stated organizational thesis is code-bearing, not load-bearing: the system asks what it knows and how that knowledge moves, rather than who holds authority over whom.

These are not the same model. S3 either reconciles them or names the departure explicitly. What it may not do is adopt her structure while keeping his language.
